misses.statement: PUT /flags/{key} with a body that declares rollout none and carries a targeting rule returns HTTP 400 whose error names that rule's id.
misses.rationale: The issue requires such a definition to be rejected with the rule's id; definitions reach the service through PUT /flags/{key}, so an operator sees the rejection there.
misses.observed: PUT /flags/demo with rollout none and rule r-1 returned HTTP 201 and stored the definition: the handler checked the body against the JSON Schema only, and flagdef.Check rejected the definition only when the evaluator later loaded it
